article.title: Mobile internet tariffs in Iran rise by 40%
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Persian article.

Iranian mobile operators MCI and Irancell have announced increases of up to 40% in the tariffs for calls, text messages, and mobile internet packages, as the government continues to impose restrictions on internet access.
The companies said in separate statements on Friday that the new rates would take effect at midnight on October 23.
Irancell has also increased the prices of its fixed internet and fiber-optic services by the same amount.
According to the operators, internet packages purchased before the new rates took effect will remain valid at their original prices until their expiration dates.
The sharp increase in internet costs comes as the Iranian government continues to impose widespread censorship and restrictions on internet access.

In its annual Freedom on the Net 2026 report, U.S.-based nonprofit Freedom House gave Iran just 9 points out of 100, placing it alongside China and Myanmar among the world’s worst countries for internet freedom.
The report said Iran experienced the steepest decline in internet freedom among the 38 countries assessed.
During the suppression of nationwide protests in January 2026, Iran almost completely shut down internet access across the country for 20 days.

In February, coinciding with the start of the joint U.S. and Israeli military operation, the government imposed another nationwide restriction on internet access that lasted approximately 88 days. The measure was described as the longest nationwide internet shutdown in Iran’s history.

Freedom House also warned that the Iranian government has turned the country’s internet into a “two-tier” system in which most citizens are denied unrestricted access to the global internet, while a limited group retains that access.

The organization also cited disruptions to Starlink satellite communications, restrictions on virtual private networks (VPNs), and the arrest of internet users. It noted that internet freedom worldwide had declined for the 16th consecutive year.

Earlier, the deputy political commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that if Iran's infrastructure were targeted, internet cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz would not be safe.

The International Cable Protection Committee said five active cable segments belonging to submarine cable systems pass through the strait, a route that carries less than 1% of the world’s international bandwidth.
According to the committee, damage to these cables would primarily disrupt regional communications.
zh: 伊朗行動網路資費上漲 40%
編者註：本報導翻譯自美國之音波斯語版原文。
隨著政府持續對網路存取實施限制，伊朗行動通訊業者 MCI 與 Irancell 已宣布將通話、簡訊及行動網路方案的資費調漲，漲幅最高達 40%。
這些公司週五分別發表聲明表示，新費率將於10月23日午夜起生效。
Irancell 亦將其固定網路及光纖服務的價格調高了相同幅度。
據營運商表示，在新資費生效前購買的網路方案，將以原價繼續有效，直至其到期日為止。
在伊朗政府持續對網路存取實施廣泛的審查與限制之際，網路費用卻急遽飆升。
總部位於美國的非營利組織「自由之家」在其年度《2026年網路自由報告》中，僅給予伊朗100分中的9分，使其與中國及緬甸並列為全球網路自由狀況最差的國家之一。
該報告指出，在受評估的 38 個國家中，伊朗的網路自由度下降幅度最大。
在2026年1月鎮壓全國性抗議活動期間，伊朗曾將全國的網路連線幾乎完全切斷長達20天。
二月間，適逢美以聯合軍事行動展開之際，政府再次實施了一項為期約88天的全國性網路限制措施。這項措施被形容為伊朗史上持續時間最長的全國性網路封鎖。
「自由之家」還警告指出，伊朗政府已將該國的網路轉變為一個「兩級」系統，在該系統中，大多數公民被剝奪了不受限制地存取全球網路的權利，而只有一小部分人仍能享有此項權利。
該組織還提到「星鏈」（Starlink）衛星通訊遭到干擾、虛擬私人網路（VPN）受到限制，以及網民遭逮捕等情況。該組織指出，全球網路自由度已連續第16年下滑。
稍早前，伊斯蘭革命衛隊（IRGC）副政治指揮官聲稱，若伊朗的基礎設施成為攻擊目標，霍爾木茲海峽底下的網路光纜將不再安全。
國際電纜保護委員會表示，有五段屬於海底電纜系統的現役電纜段穿越該海峽，這條路線承載的國際頻寬佔全球總量的不到1%。
據該委員會表示，這些電纜若受損，主要將導致區域通訊中斷。
